pr_title: gh-89739: gh-77140: Support zip64 in zipimport
pr_body:
* Reads zip64 files as produced by the zipfile module
* Include tests (somewhat slow, however, because of the need to create "large" zips)
* About the same amount of strictness reading invalid zip files as zipfile has
* Still works on files with prepended data (like pex)

There are a lot more test cases at https://github.com/thatch/zipimport64/ that give me confidence that this works for real-world files.  I assume this relnotes worthy, let me know any other followups you'd like.

As an aside, in its current state can be applied as a patch at least as far back as 3.8, as long as you regenerate frozen modules.  I don't expect cpython to do this, but I certainly will on our internal version.

Fixes #89739 and #77140

pr_comments: One question I've got is whether the only exception zipimport is allowed to raise is `ZipImportError` or if that's just leftover from the C implementation.  The calls to `.pop(0)` can raise `IndexError` but there may be other non-`ZipImportError` and I haven't fuzzed it.
`zipimport` can raise whatever exceptions makes sense. `ZipImportError` is specific to custom exceptions that `zipimport` needs to raise.

---

Side note: Please don't assume any specific committer can dedicate their volunteer interrupt time to your needs and that some people have more important priorities; for example https://twitter.com/SerhiyStorchaka/status/1579376282252742656 (and more recent sad news).

> Would it make sense to add a `_zipfile` module to share code between zipfile and zipimport? I expect that some code is in common, no?

That kind of refactoring deserves its own issue, it isn't in scope here. You can construct an interpreter with a zipped up standard library if you add zipimport to your bootstrap. Adding dependencies gets complicated. Otherwise zipimport would just use zipfile directly already. See the https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/69897 discussion when the old C zipimport was rewritten into this Python one.

> That kind of refactoring deserves its own issue, it isn't in scope here.

I expect that the review should be easier if changes specific to zipimport are smaller, if more code is shared between zipimport and zipfile.

>  Adding dependencies gets complicated.

Why is it complicated? _zipimport (common code) should be designed to be usable at Python startup, by zipimport. The code which doesn't fit with Python startup should stay in zipfile.

For example, I see that many constants are the same between the two files. Can't they be shared?

```
END_CENTRAL_DIR_SIZE = 22
END_CENTRAL_DIR_SIZE_64 = 56
END_CENTRAL_DIR_LOCATOR_SIZE_64 = 20
STRING_END_ARCHIVE = b'PK\x05\x06'  # standard EOCD signature
STRING_END_LOCATOR_64 = b'PK\x06\x07'  # Zip64 EOCD Locator signature
STRING_END_ZIP_64 = b'PK\x06\x06'  # Zip64 EOCD signature
MAX_COMMENT_LEN = (1 << 16) - 1
MAX_UINT32 = 0xffffffff
ZIP64_EXTRA_TAG = 0x1
```

Well, I'm just talking for myself. If someone else is available to review such large change, please go ahead with the proposed design ;-)

>> Adding dependencies gets complicated.
> Why is it complicated? _zipimport (common code) should be designed to be usable at Python startup, by zipimport. The code which doesn't fit with Python startup should stay in zipfile.

It's adding one more frozen module, but those are cheap and plentiful these days.  The constants are one thing, but the logic would be even better to unify.  For example, zipimport doesn't verify crc (which makes https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/63281 easier to hit).  That's a bigger project that I can look at for 3.13, but there are almost certainly behavior changes involved (around which one is chosen for duplicated member names, for one).

This needs updating and zipimport merge conflicts resolved.  Given 3.12beta1 happens Monday lets assume this is already missing 3.12 and targeting 3.13 so the versionchanged also needs updating.

That also gives us more time to reconsider if we should do some refactoring to share anything common a new _zipimport frozen module as @vstinner was suggesting.

I won't have time to look at this for a several more weeks, but the one thing in the back of my mind about the zipimport implementation is... for import purposes, we should probably be pedantic about the zip format:

Anytime zip allows there to be multiple directory entries or copies of directory information referring to the same file we should ensure that all of them exist as expected and are in agreement.  I haven't looked to see if the current code _already_ does this (central directory vs per file header) - zip64 might provide another opportunity for that kind of shenanigan? _(I have to reread and refresh myself on zip format specifics anytime I dive in on such code)_

I'm thinking of this from a security perspective: we don't want zip files that zipimport's implementation happens to interpret in a different way than any other zip file reader implementation as that could provide ways to potentially hide code.

---

Overall: thanks for everybody's work on this, we'll eventually get it in.

> zip64 might provide another opportunity for that kind of shenanigan?

If you're asking if this is one more branch case that decompressors could handle differently, the answer is "yes."  I don't know whether that's a blocker in my mind -- even unifying the two python libs would still have differences when compared with e.g. the "unzip" command on *nix.

I've tried to import a module from a fat jar file and got a ModuleNotFoundError: No module named ... error.

I checked that the jar file had more than 65k files and was created using Zip64. When I unzip the file, Python is capable of importing the modules.

I was able to reproduce the error on a simple project, such as:

simplePackage/
  \_\_init__.py
  a/
    \_\_init__.py
    moduleA.py

where

- I'm using Python 3.9.4
- \_\_init__.py files are empty
- moduleA.py only has a printA() function

I ran the following tests:

1. When importing from the folder, it works

```pycon
python
>>> import sys
>>> sys.path.append('C:\\Users\\...\\simplePackage')
>>> from a.moduleA import printA
>>> printA()
I'm module a
```


2. When zipping the folder, it works

```pycon
python
>>> import sys
>>> sys.path.append('C:\\Users\\...\\simplePackage.zip')
>>> from a.moduleA import printA
>>> printA()
I'm module a
```


3. When forcing to zip with Zip64 it doesn't work

On linux: zip -fzr simple64Package.zip .

```pycon
python
>>> import sys
>>> sys.path.append('C:\\Users\\...\\simple64Package.zip')
>>> from a.moduleA import printA
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'a'
```


Is this an expected behavior? Am I missing something?

Thanks!
